description: Basepan Space Challenge Team: Victor Chisom Muojeke, Amalraj Rajesh, Chiemerie Cletus Obijiaku and Olaleye Adeniyi Akinuli. We built NL Fire Calendar, a web app that joins NASA MODIS and VIIRS fire detections into one consistent burning-activity calendar for Newfoundland and Labrador, with area and date selection, a zoomable map, CSV downloads and a carbon monoxide smoke tab.
summary:
What we developed: NL Fire Calendar, a free web app that merges NASA's two satellite fire records, MODIS (2000 onward) and VIIRS (2012 onward), into one burning-activity calendar for Newfoundland and Labrador. 
How it meets the challenge: MODIS is being retired, and its counts cannot be directly compared with VIIRS counts. We count "fire cells" (a 0.1 degree square with a detection on one day), calculate one multiplier from the 14 seasons where both sensors overlap, and adjust the older MODIS months to the VIIRS level. A user picks an area and dates, sees how the latest month compares with the same month in other years, and downloads the data and pictures. A Canadian Space Agency carbon monoxide tab adds smoke context. 
Why it matters: about 10 years of fire history stay usable for land managers and scientists. We tested the merge (about 15% error for a season) and state its limits on screen.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

NL Fire Calendar puts NASA's two satellite fire records, MODIS (2000 on) and VIIRS (2012 on), on one scale for Newfoundland and Labrador. The user picks an area (draw it on a zoomable map, or type latitude and longitude) and a month range, presses Apply, and gets a calendar (years by months) and a "Right now" box that compares the latest month with the same month in other years.

To merge the sensors, we count "fire cells" (a 0.1 degree square with a detection on one day), calculate one multiplier (1.615) from the 14 May to September seasons where both sensors overlap, and scale the older MODIS months to the VIIRS level. A Smoke tab adds monthly carbon monoxide from the Canadian Space Agency's MOPITT instrument, as context. Users can download the hotspots, the monthly counts and the charts.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

MODIS is being retired, so about 10 years of fire history could be lost. This keeps it usable for land managers and scientists, and shows in plain words whether the latest month is busy or quiet compared with other years.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

Counting fire cells instead of raw hotspots stops VIIRS's finer pixels from inflating counts. Each month is compared only with years from the same sensor period, so merged and unmerged years never mix. The page shows its own error and limits on screen.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

We tested the merge by predicting each season from the others: about 15% median error for a season and about 60% for a single month. One province-wide multiplier does not hold for small areas, so the app shows the local one. The app gives historical context only: no forecasts, alerts, confirmed fires or burned area. We also made it work with a keyboard, with colourblind-safe colours, and on a phone.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib) for the data pipeline. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the app, with no outside libraries. pytest and Playwright for more than 330 automated tests. GitHub Pages for hosting.

Code: https://github.com/portalzone/nl-fire-calendar

Live app: https://portalzone.github.io/nl-fire-calendar/

DATA

NASA FIRMS (MODIS Collection 6.1; VIIRS 375 m from Suomi NPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21) and CSA MOPITT carbon monoxide.

TEAM

Basepan Space Challenge Team: Victor Chisom Muojeke, Amalraj Rajesh, Chiemerie Cletus Obijiaku and Olaleye Adeniyi Akinuli.

USE OF AI

The code, tests and documentation in this project were written with the help of AI tools: an AI coding assistant (Claude, by Anthropic) and GitHub Copilot. The team reviewed, ran and tested them. No AI-generated images, video or audio are used.
